description: The rise of the Mexica people from wandering migrants to rulers of the largest empire in pre-Columbian Mesoamerica — its founding cities, rulers, conquests, and engineering achievements, through its fall to the Spanish.

events.title: The Mexica depart Aztlán
events.desc: According to Aztec tradition, the Mexica people set out from a legendary homeland called Aztlán, beginning a long migration south into the Valley of Mexico. Aztlán's exact location, if it existed as a real place, remains uncertain.

events.title: Tenochtitlan founded
events.desc: Wandering Mexica settlers built their city on a marshy island in Lake Texcoco after seeing an eagle perched on a cactus — a sign their priests had said would mark the end of their migration. Tenochtitlan grew into the capital of the Aztec Empire.

events.title: Tlatelolco founded
events.desc: A splinter group of Mexica settled a second island just north of Tenochtitlan, founding a sister city that became one of the greatest markets in the Americas.

events.title: Acamapichtli becomes the first tlatoani
events.desc: Tenochtitlan's elders chose Acamapichtli, a noble with Toltec and Tepanec ancestry, as their first tlatoani (ruler), founding the dynasty that would lead the Aztec Empire.

events.title: Huitzilihuitl becomes the second tlatoani
events.desc: Acamapichtli's son strengthened Tenochtitlan's position through marriage alliances with neighboring city-states, including the powerful Tepanec capital of Azcapotzalco.

events.title: Chimalpopoca becomes the third tlatoani
events.desc: Still a tributary of the Tepanec Empire, Tenochtitlan continued to grow under its third ruler, who was killed amid a succession struggle with Azcapotzalco around 1426.

events.title: Itzcoatl becomes the fourth tlatoani
events.desc: Itzcoatl, an uncle of the murdered Chimalpopoca, took power and moved quickly to end Tenochtitlan's subjugation to the Tepanecs.

events.title: Defeat of Azcapotzalco; the Triple Alliance formed
events.desc: Tenochtitlan, Texcoco, and Tlacopan united to defeat the dominant Tepanec capital of Azcapotzalco. The resulting Triple Alliance became the political foundation of what is now called the Aztec Empire.

events.title: Tlacaelel reorganizes the empire
events.desc: As cihuacoatl (chief advisor), Tlacaelel restructured Mexica religion, law, and government, elevating the war god Huitzilopochtli and reshaping the ideology that fueled decades of imperial expansion.

events.title: Moctezuma I becomes the fifth tlatoani
events.desc: Moctezuma I (Ilhuicamina) expanded the empire significantly and undertook major public works to strengthen Tenochtitlan's island capital.

events.title: Great famine strikes the Valley of Mexico
events.desc: A severe multi-year famine, worsened by drought and frost, devastated the Valley of Mexico. Some accounts describe families selling children into slavery for food during the worst years.

events.title: Nezahualcoyotl's dike completed
events.desc: The poet-king of Texcoco, an ally in the Triple Alliance, engineered a massive stone dike across Lake Texcoco to separate its salty and fresh waters and control flooding, protecting Tenochtitlan's chinampa farmland.

events.title: Conquest of Chalco completed
events.desc: After decades of intermittent conflict, Moctezuma I's forces fully subdued the Chalco region southeast of Tenochtitlan, securing valuable farmland and labor.

events.title: Chapultepec aqueduct completed
events.desc: A dual-channel aqueduct was built to carry fresh spring water from the hill of Chapultepec into Tenochtitlan, allowing the channels to be cleaned and repaired without cutting off the city's water supply.

events.title: Axayacatl becomes the sixth tlatoani
events.desc: A grandson of Moctezuma I, Axayacatl continued the empire's military expansion and commissioned some of its best-known monuments.

events.title: Axayacatl conquers Tlatelolco
events.desc: After years as a rival trading center, Tlatelolco was defeated and absorbed under direct Tenochtitlan rule, uniting the two island cities.

events.title: Defeat by the Tarascan Empire
events.desc: In one of the Aztec Empire's rare major military defeats, a large Aztec army was routed by the Tarascans (Purépecha) near the western frontier, halting Aztec expansion in that direction for good.

events.title: The Sun Stone is carved
events.desc: A massive basalt disc carved with a cosmological calendar — later known as the Aztec Calendar Stone or Sun Stone — was created under Axayacatl, likely as a monument rather than a working calendar.

events.title: Tizoc becomes the seventh tlatoani
events.desc: Tizoc's brief and militarily unsuccessful reign is remembered mainly for the Tizoc Stone, a carved monument commemorating his campaigns.

events.title: Ahuitzotl becomes the eighth tlatoani
events.desc: Ahuitzotl proved a far more aggressive military leader than his predecessor, driving the empire to its greatest territorial extent.

events.title: Great Temple dedicated
events.desc: Ahuitzotl presided over the dedication of an expanded Templo Mayor in Tenochtitlan, marked by a mass ceremony of human sacrifice that chroniclers describe as enormous in scale, though the exact numbers are disputed by modern historians.

events.title: Conquest of Xoconochco
events.desc: Ahuitzotl's forces pushed the empire's reach to Xoconochco on the Pacific coast near modern Guatemala, a distant province valued for cacao and exotic feathers.

events.title: Moctezuma II becomes the ninth tlatoani
events.desc: Moctezuma II inherited an empire at its territorial peak, ruling over millions of people across central Mexico when Spanish ships first arrived on the coast.

events.title: Cortés meets Moctezuma II in Tenochtitlan
events.desc: Hernán Cortés and his expedition, joined by thousands of Indigenous allies hostile to Aztec rule, entered Tenochtitlan and were received by Moctezuma II, who was soon taken hostage in his own palace.

events.title: Massacre in the Great Temple
events.desc: While Cortés was away, his deputy Pedro de Alvarado ordered an attack on unarmed Mexica nobles during the Toxcatl festival, triggering a citywide uprising against the Spanish.

events.title: La Noche Triste; death of Moctezuma II
events.desc: Besieged and facing open revolt, Moctezuma II died in disputed circumstances, and the Spanish were forced to flee Tenochtitlan at night, suffering heavy losses crossing the city's causeways.

events.title: Cuitláhuac becomes the tenth tlatoani
events.desc: Moctezuma's brother organized the successful defense that drove the Spanish from the city, but his reign lasted only weeks.

events.title: Smallpox epidemic devastates Tenochtitlan
events.desc: A smallpox epidemic, introduced by the Spanish and their expedition, swept through the city with catastrophic effect, killing Cuitláhuac and a huge share of the population just as the empire needed to rebuild its defenses.

events.title: Cuauhtémoc becomes the eleventh and final tlatoani
events.desc: A young cousin of Moctezuma II, Cuauhtémoc took the throne amid epidemic and war, and led the last defense of Tenochtitlan against the Spanish and their Indigenous allies.

events.title: Fall of Tenochtitlan
events.desc: After a brutal months-long siege that starved and devastated the city, Spanish forces and tens of thousands of Indigenous allies captured Tenochtitlan, ending the Aztec Empire and beginning Spanish colonial rule over central Mexico.
